Take a quiet stretch with someone close and stay with what's already settled between you. Don't fix it, explain it, or turn it into the next thing. You'll know the difference between a feeling that's finished and one that's merely restful. Let the finished ones stay finished around you.
1.sheetLine: You can sit inside feeling that's already run its course.

2.tense: Somewhere down the road the whole thing is being finished before it's been lived.
2.verb: letting the whole of what you've felt settle into something you can hold
2.place: the ground where you're becoming what you already are
2.ask: Before you pour yourself into the next feeling, say in a line what it's for. Decide that first, then hold a day before spending anything on it.
2.core:
A feeling shows up and your mind is already at the far end of it — how it lands, what it means, how it closes. You're rehearsing the arc before the first sentence is spoken. It's not that you're racing the feeling; you're standing over it, holding a shape it hasn't taken yet.

The pull is toward the finished version: the resolved talk, the settled thing, the heart caught up before it's had its day. That bracing leaves nothing to recognize — the moment arrives and you've already been there. Before you pour yourself into the next feeling, say in a line what it's for. Decide that first, then hold a day before spending anything on it. Wholeness doesn't arrive early; it waits until the thing has been lived, and it keeps deepening after that.
2.sheetLine: You're finishing the feeling before it's had its day.

3.tense: You stood at the door where this would close, and you're still standing there now.
3.verb: letting the whole of what you've felt settle into something you can hold
3.place: the ground where you're becoming what you already are
3.ask: Let a small impulse that's been waiting start today, without deciding yet what it's for. No plan, no point, no finish line.
3.core:
The place where you're becoming what you are has gone quiet. Feeling is there, but nothing in you reaches to feel it through to the end, so conversations stay half-finished and closeness stays half-had. You can remember knowing what your heart knows. You're not standing in it.

Pushing feeling in won't do anything. What wakes it is starting something that isn't pointed yet. Let a small impulse that's been waiting start today — a call, a beginning, a small thing — without deciding what it's for. No plan, no point, no finish line. The point is the spark, not the shape. That knowing comes back unprompted once something in you is moving; it returns to a person who still has the whole spectrum in them and no longer needs it finished to touch it.
3.sheetLine: Nothing reaches to feel it through, so things stay half-finished.

4.tense: You've been keeping the accounts fair for everyone, and you'd say they're just balanced now.
4.verb: letting the whole of what you've felt settle into something you can hold
4.place: the ground where you're becoming what you already are
4.ask: Return what you owe someone — the call, the thanks, the bit of care you've been carrying but not mentioning. Before anyone asks for it.
4.core:
The fairness rolling through you is yours, and the version you tell is that things just kept being balanced. You kept them fair. People come out even around you, and the work is invisible, including to you.

Before all this, fairness was simple: something owed, something paid. Return what you owe someone — the call, the thanks, the bit of care you've been carrying but not mentioning — before anyone asks for it. The compass you've been operating by gets a face again. The completion that's already here isn't a report; it's a habit of making things even that you've been running without calling it yours.
4.sheetLine: Things stay fair around you, and you'd call it just how they are.

1.tense: You are here at the page and the entire shape is in view.
1.verb: Seeing the whole shape at once
1.place: Standing outside the pattern while still inside it
1.ask: Take ten quiet minutes and sit with one thing your heart already knows about a whole in your life. Draw no conclusion and fix nothing.
1.core:
You're standing where all of it can be taken in. What was in pieces has come together into one shape you can hold without reaching for the next move. It stays steady because the picture is genuinely yours — you aren't checking it against anyone else's version. Inside this, what you feel and what you know don't need separating, and today they aren't separated.

The long stretch of feeling your way through this is what bought the view, and the next move isn't more of that. Sit with what the heart already knows, before any plan gets built on top. Ten quiet minutes with one whole thing — no conclusion drawn, no repair queued, just the picture you're already carrying. If nothing further gets done about it, that's the week working.
1.sheetLine: You can see the whole of it from here.

2.tense: You are bracing against an ending that has not arrived.
2.verb: Seeing the whole shape at once
2.place: Standing outside the pattern while still inside it
2.ask: Before you act on the pattern, write a single line saying what this whole thing is for. Then act from that line, not from the pull.
2.core:
The shape is barely in view and you're already writing past it. You've called it finished in your head, or close enough, and you're rehearsing how it will land — how you'll say it, what will change, how the other will take it. Nothing has happened yet. The conclusion is doing all the work, and it's running ahead of what's actually here.

Seeing it early isn't the problem; acting from the early seeing is. Decide what this is for before you spend anything on it: one line, written before the move, about what the whole thing is meant to serve. Then let that line steer, not the pull of a finished story. If the line turns out wrong, you'll know within the week — cheaper than moving on a conclusion the situation hasn't earned.
2.sheetLine: You're reading an ending that isn't here yet.

3.tense: You stood at a threshold that is behind you now and did not cross.
3.verb: Seeing the whole shape at once
3.place: Standing outside the pattern while still inside it
3.ask: Begin something with no name yet — a page, a call, a walk — and don't decide what it's for until it has already started.
3.core:
A threshold has passed and you're on the far side of it, still facing it. The whole thing came near enough to be seen, and you stayed outside — not refusing, just not arriving. The shape is there and you aren't in it, and the not-arriving has begun to harden into a habit.

Stop trying to see the whole of it again. Begin the thing while it is still nothing in particular: an unnamed move, no plan and no outcome attached, and hold off deciding what it's for until it has already started. It doesn't have to be about the threshold that passed; it only has to be in the present tense. Green things come up without knowing what they are first. Sight returns when there's something here for it to fall on.
3.sheetLine: The threshold is behind you and you're still facing it.

4.tense: You are already reading how it all fits together and not signing the reading.
4.verb: Seeing the whole shape at once
4.place: Standing outside the pattern while still inside it
4.ask: When your read of a situation tells you what's owed, do that thing the same day — no case, no announcement. Notice afterward that you did it.
4.core:
You can already see how it fits together. Mid-conversation you know what's fair here, what's owed, what the next right move is — and you say the group just works well, or that anyone would notice the same thing. The reading is yours. When you describe it, you describe the air, and the read you keep disowning is the read that's steering.

The next time the read points at what's right, go do that thing that day. Quietly, no case made, no review afterward — just the act your own read indicated. Using the compass is what makes it yours to hold. If you're wrong that this is your gift, you've spent a day being fair and gained nothing to regret.
4.sheetLine: You're already reading it. You just won't sign it.

1.tense: The feeling has settled into its own depth and is here to be rested in.
1.verb: feeling the whole arc of it, and knowing the feeling itself as already whole
1.place: at the edge of a finished thing, where what's held is released into what comes next
1.ask: Set aside one unhurried stretch and sit with what you feel about someone close, without turning it into a conversation, a plan, or a fix.
1.core:
You're in a stretch where the feeling has caught up with what you know. The full range of it is available, and you're not in a hurry to move it along — the whole of it can sit there without needing to be said out loud. People notice this and reach for it. You're not bracing for anything.

What this balance is free to do next is let it keep deepening while you're not steering it. Set a real moment aside and sit with what you feel about someone close to you. No conversation, no fix, no task attached. Nothing has to come of it. What shows up when you stay put a while is different from what shows up mid-conversation, and you can find that out by staying put.
1.sheetLine: The feeling has caught up with what you know.

2.tense: The ending keeps getting pushed to a point beyond the one you're standing in.
2.verb: feeling the whole arc of it, and knowing the feeling itself as already whole
2.place: at the edge of a finished thing, where what's held is released into what comes next
2.ask: Before you put anything more into the thing that's ending, hold the next pay-off in your hand for a day — unspent, uncommitted, not yet named.
2.core:
You can feel the arc closing, and instead of standing in the close, you're reaching past it — deciding what the end will have meant before the end arrives. Anything unfinished gets covered with an explanation, and the explanation gets treated as the completion. That's a lot of energy spent on a future you can't write in yet, and the present part of the ending goes unfelt.

What's needed is direction that lands where you actually are. Before you hand anything else to this thing, hold the first return you get from it for a day without spending it or naming what it's for. Let it exist in your hand. The end has its own shape, and deciding that shape early is the thing keeping you from living it.
2.sheetLine: You're deciding what the ending means before it arrives.

3.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you.
3.verb: feeling the whole arc of it, and knowing the feeling itself as already whole
3.place: at the edge of a finished thing, where what's held is released into what comes next
3.ask: Catch the first small pull toward something new and follow it one step before you name what it's for.
3.core:
Where you are in this cycle, the ending has already happened, and your attention hasn't come out of it. You keep describing what closed rather than what's next, and so the completion doesn't quite release you into anything. Nothing has lit up in you toward the next thing yet. The door is behind you; your face is still turned toward it.

Energy is what this needs, and it comes from the smallest available spark rather than a decision. Catch the first pull toward something new and follow it one step before you've decided what it's for. No assignment, no point, just the beginning of a beginning. The new thing will catch once something in you starts moving.

It doesn't have to mean anything.
3.sheetLine: Your face is still toward the door you already passed.

4.tense: The completion is being carried out in you without your name on it.
4.verb: feeling the whole arc of it, and knowing the feeling itself as already whole
4.place: at the edge of a finished thing, where what's held is released into what comes next
4.ask: Where a small wrong sits close this week, act on what you sense is right — do it, and don't make the case afterward.
4.core:
You know what an ending owes people. The felt sense of what's fair — what's been given, what's still owed, when to close a thing cleanly — is operating in you all the time, and the work it does is steady. But you keep the account under the table, and when someone asks how you arrived at a decision, you say it just felt right and stop there.

What returns it to you is doing one small right thing where the compass, not a calculation, is what moves you. Act on it plainly this week. Don't argue the case, don't explain the reasoning, don't defend the call. It was already yours. Doing it without the argument is how you stop being surprised by how well you already understood.
4.sheetLine: You know what an ending owes, and you keep the account to yourself.
